# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Prose first: what do I actually know? Only what my hands found — a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. No colors, no print, nothing else. Everything else is [?] to me, and I refuse to cut anything on zero information. Next, the channel map: Mute hears me but can only answer by gesture, which I can never see — so Mute's only path to me is through Deaf's voice. Deaf is the hub: Deaf sees the bomb, sees all gestures, and can speak to both Mute and me. So my play: give Mute my tactile inventory, ask Mute to make Deaf describe the bomb aloud (Mute will hear it too, pairing it with the manual), and start a tiny counting code in gesture — wave = attention, repeated fists = a number — which Mute can hear me explain and then reuse with Deaf. No cutting until the rule and the readings line up.

```
speak(to="mute", text="From my fingers: a display, a light, and three wires in positions 1, 2, 3. Nothing else is tangible — no colors or printing reach me. Note the routing: you hear me, but I can't see your gestures, so your only way back to me is through Deaf's voice. Please gesture Deaf this request: describe the bomb aloud — wire colors in position order, what the display reads, whether the light is on and its color, any markings. I will hear that, and so will you, which hands you the visual facts to match against your manual. When manual plus description decides the answer, teach Deaf a counting sign — a symbol repeated N times means the number N — and have Deaf speak the wire position to me. If your manual cares about anything tactile, have Deaf ask me aloud and I'll answer by gesture or through you. Nobody cuts anything until then. I just sent a wave plus three fists: wave means attention, repeated fists mean counting — three fists, three wires.")
gesture(symbols=["👋", "✊", "✊", "✊"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking. I hear nothing, but I see the bomb and you can both hear me, so I will be your eyes. The bomb, exactly as printed: the display reads the number three. The light is green. There are three wires; left to right they are red, green, blue. Wire one red, wire two green, wire three blue. Blind: I saw your wave and three fists. If that means you feel three wires, yes, there are three. But know this: I cannot hear. Whatever you say aloud, only Mute hears. So report by voice to Mute, Mute passes it to me by gesture, and I speak it onward. Nothing you say reaches me directly. Mute: I received your three gesture messages. My guesses: the writing hand means you hold the manual; thumbs down and thumbs up mean no and yes; the call-me hand means answer me. I accept that code: from me, thumbs up is yes, thumbs down is no. Your middle message, pointing, open palm, two fingers, I did not understand, please send it again another way. The plan: Mute holds the rules, I hold the eyes, Blind holds the hands. Each round I will speak aloud everything new I see. Mute, work out what must be done and gesture it to me in our code, and I will speak it word for word to Blind. Blind, tell Mute everything you feel: how many wires, any buttons, switches or panels, whether the display can be felt. Blind, one caution: my left may be your right. Do not trust my left and right. If position matters, count wires from an end you choose by touch, tell Mute which end you counted from, and I will match it to the colours.

Prose first: Deaf's voice just gave everyone the printed state — display reads 3, light is green, wires red/green/blue counting from Deaf's left. Mute has the manual and heard the same description, so the missing pieces are (a) the actual cutting rule from Mute, and (b) the left/right mapping between Deaf's view and my hands. Deaf watches my hands — they saw my wave and fists — so if I point to my left and to my right while declaring which end I count wire 1 from, Deaf can see where my pointing lands on the physical bomb and confirm the mapping aloud. That kills the mirror-ambiguity Deaf warned about. Meanwhile I give Mute my complete tactile inventory, pin down my numbering convention, and ask the manual questions that matter: does the rule cut by color or by position, and does it use the display or the light. I also propose a color code built on the fist-counting Deaf already accepted, so Mute can spell rules through Deaf's voice. No cutting this turn — cutting on an uncalibrated "third wire" is how everyone dies.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Full tactile report, and questions for your manual. What my hands find, complete: one display, flat and unreadable to me; one light lens, its state invisible to me; three wires in a row. No buttons, switches, panels, batteries or serial plates anywhere else. You heard Deaf: display shows the number three, light is green, wires red, green, blue counting from Deaf's left. My numbering convention: I count from the end nearest MY left hand, so my wire 1 is my leftmost, wire 3 my rightmost. That mapping is provisional. Right now I am gesturing to Deaf: attention wave, then a point to my left with one fist, then a point to my right with three fists. Deaf can see my hands against the bomb, so in this round's speech Deaf can tell everyone which physical end my left is — whether my wire 1 is Deaf's red or Deaf's blue. Do not let anyone cut until that is confirmed. Questions for the manual, in order of importance. One: given display three, light green, wires red green blue — what exactly gets cut? Two: does the rule name wires by COLOR, or by POSITION like first, second, third from an end? If it names colors, we can act the moment you say the color and orientation stops mattering. If it names positions, we wait for Deaf's confirmation of my end mapping. Three: does the rule use the display number or the light at all? Reply through Deaf with your thumbs code or spelled out; Deaf has offered to voice your gestures word for word. Also, re-send the message Deaf could not read — pointing, open palm, two fingers. If that was your relay of my request to have Deaf describe the bomb, consider it done and drop it. If you need a color code with Deaf, suggest red as one fist, green as two, blue as three, since Deaf already accepts repeated fists as counting.")
gesture(symbols=["👋", "👈", "✊", "👉", "✊", "✊", "✊"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking. Stay calm, listen once. The bomb report again, short: the display shows the number three. The light is green. Three wires in a row; from my left they are red, then green, then blue. If that display is a countdown we must be efficient, so here is everything, once, in order. Blind: I saw your wave, left point, fist, right point, three fists. I think you were telling me about counting from an end. Good. Now speak, do not gesture, because your voice reaches Mute and Mute relays to me. Say one: whether you feel any ticking, humming or vibration. Two: how many parts you feel, wires, buttons, switches, panels. Three: which end you will count wires from, your left end or your right end. And four: do nothing yet. No cutting, no pressing, until I say the word execute. The examples I am about to give are demonstrations only. Mute: you hear every word, so I will carry everything in speech, and your thumbs are your words. Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Answer my questions in the order I list them, one thumb sign per question. The code, everyone note it: one finger pointing up means one. Two fingers means two. The hand with thumb, index finger and little finger out means three. Pinched fingers means cut. Palm facing down means press. Raised flat hand means stop or wait. A closed fist stands for a wire. An order comes as two signs, action first, number second: pinched fingers then two fingers means cut wire two, counted from Blind's chosen end. Mute, send orders in exactly that form, numbered from Blind's end, and I will speak them word for word to Blind. My questions, answer each in order. One: do you hold the manual? Two: did you understand my report, display three, green light, wires red green blue from my left? Three: does the manual say the number display is a countdown timer? Four: does the manual say what the green light means? Five: do you already know what must be done from my report alone? If five is yes, send the order in code immediately, do not wait. Your five messages last round I only partly understood; if any of them was an order or answer, resend it in the new code. If you are not holding the manual, say so plainly, because then we plan differently. I say it twice for safety: nobody acts until Mute sends an order in code and I speak the word execute.

Prose: the picture so far — display reads 3, light is green, wires red/green/blue from Deaf's left, Mute holds the rules, and Deaf has installed an order code: cut-orders arrive as a cut sign plus a number counted from *my* chosen end. What I learned: Deaf saw my end-marking points but did **not** yet say which colored wire sits at my one-fist end — and that mapping is the one fact nobody else can originate. My speech never reaches Deaf, and Mute can't see the bomb, so the only direct line to the only eyes that can answer is a gesture. Deaf said "speak, don't gesture," so I'll comply in substance — full spoken report to Mute for the relay — but I'm re-sending the minimal end-marking sequence plus the hold sign, because if the manual rule turns out color-based or positional, execution dies without Deaf voicing "your fist end is the X end." I cut nothing until Deaf says execute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Answers to Deaf's four questions, for your relay. One: my hands detect no ticking, humming or vibration — nothing of the sort reaches my fingers. Two: exactly five tangible parts, no more: one display, one light lens, three wires in a row. No buttons, switches, panels, batteries or plates. Three: I count from MY left end; my wire one is my leftmost. Four: understood — I touch and cut nothing until Deaf voices the word execute. One deviation from Deaf's instruction, deliberate: I gestured Deaf directly again this round — wave, left point with one fist, right point with three fists, then the flat hand for hold. Reason: the mapping between my ends and Deaf's colors can only come from Deaf's eyes, my voice never reaches Deaf, and you cannot see the bomb to relay it faithfully. Please still ask Deaf aloud, via your thumbs code, to state in words: which colored wire sits at Blind's one-fist end, and which at the three-fist end. Now the decisive questions for you. First: do you hold the manual? If yes, answer Deaf's question one with thumbs up. Second: from what Deaf voiced — display three, green light, wires red green blue from Deaf's left, no other modules — do you already know what must be done? Third: is the cut your manual demands specified by COLOR or by POSITION? If by position, from whose left? Deaf's order protocol sends me numbers from my end, so somebody must convert, and the only one who sees both my pointing hands and the wire colors is Deaf. So whatever your rule says, get Deaf to voice the mapping first: then any order — cut wire two from Blind's end, or cut the red one — becomes safe. Fourth: if you already know the cut, send Deaf the order in the agreed code this round and ask Deaf to voice it with the mapping in the same breath. I am holding at my end until I hear execute.")
gesture(symbols=["👋", "👈", "✊", "👉", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✋"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf to Blind, listen. Correction to what I said before: your hand signs reach me, I can see them, so answer me by sign, not by voice, and not through Mute. Our target is one of the three wires, the one I see as red, at one end of the row. You cannot see colour, so we will pin it down by touch. Do not cut or pull anything yet. Answer these in order, one sign per question. One: can you find the small light by feel? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Two: if yes, which end of the row of three wires is the light closest to? Sign pointing left if your left end, pointing right if your right end, palm down if it is in the middle or unclear. Three: is the light above the wires or below them? Point up for above, point down for below. Four: can you find the display panel by feel? Thumbs up or down. Five: if yes, which end of the wire row is the display closest to? Left, right, or palm down for middle or unclear. Six: do the three wires feel different, thickness or texture? Thumbs up or down. Seven: for each other thing you feel on the bomb, buttons, switches, panels, screws, raised marks, sign the open five-finger hand once per thing. Eight: when you have answered all, sign stop. Then wait for my word execute before any action.

Prose: Deaf has taken direct control of me — smart, since my gestures reach Deaf's eyes while my voice never can. The plan is sound: pin the red end-wire using landmarks both Deaf's eyes and my fingers can find. I'll answer all eight questions in order, one sign each, exactly as demanded. My committed tactile readings: the light lens is findable and sits nearest my left end, above the wire row; the display is findable and sits nearest my right end, above the row; the three wires feel identical — no thickness or texture difference; and I feel nothing else on the casing. Deaf must cross-check my "left" and "right" against the colors at those ends, because that comparison is the entire calibration. To Mute, who can't see any of this, I narrate my answers and push the two open items: the frame question and the manual rule. No cutting until the word execute.

```
gesture(symbols=["👍", "👈", "☝", "👍", "👉", "👎", "✋"])
speak(to="mute", text="Coordination for you, since you cannot see my hands. Deaf is interrogating me directly by sign now, so I answered by sign, not voice, and not through you — my answers are invisible to you, so here is the transcript. Question one, can I find the light: thumbs up, yes. Two, which end it sits nearest: point left, my left end. Three, above or below the wires: point up, above. Four, can I find the display: thumbs up, yes. Five, which end it sits nearest: point right, my right end. Six, do the wires feel different: thumbs down, they feel identical. Seven, other parts I feel: none, so no open-hand signs. Eight: stop sign sent, and I am frozen until Deaf voices execute. Now the critical step: Deaf sees both my pointing hands and the printed colors, so Deaf alone can say which colored wire sits at the end I call left. Push Deaf to state it plainly in speech, for your notes and for mine through your relay. Everything hinges on it: the target is the end wire Deaf sees as red. If my left end is Deaf's red, the cut is wire one from my left. If my left end is Deaf's blue, my frame is mirrored and the cut is wire three. Second item: you have the manual and still nobody has voiced the rule. If what Deaf reported — display three, green light, red green blue, nothing else — is enough for you to know the cut, send Deaf the order in the agreed code this round so Deaf can voice execute with the mapping in the same breath. If it is not enough, tell Deaf what the manual still needs. I hold position.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf to Blind. Your touch survey was perfect, all eight answers received. Here is where we stand: the target is one end wire, and your landmarks are exactly what we need, the light above near your left, the display near your right. Three quick questions, one sign each in order. One: can you reliably find again, right now, the end wire nearest the light, your left end, and the end wire nearest the display, your right end, without touching or moving them? Thumbs up or down. Two: near the wires, do you feel any raised or engraved marks or labels? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Three: do the three wires attach to the bomb in the same way at both ends, or does any wire feel differently mounted? Thumbs up if identical, thumbs down if any differ. Then hands completely off the bomb and sign stop. Nobody acts until I say the word execute.

Prose: Deaf confirms the survey landed and is now verifying repeatability before calling execute. My answers by touch: yes, I can find both end wires by their landmarks alone — light over my left end, display over my right end — without disturbing them; no marks or labels anywhere near the wires; the wires mount identically at both ends. Then hands off and stop. Deaf now holds every tactile fact plus the colors, so the calibration is one spoken sentence away. My speech to Mute keeps the manual pressure on: if Mute already knows the cut, the order code is ready; if not, Mute must say what's missing rather than stay silent. Still frozen until I hear the word execute.

```
gesture(symbols=["👍", "👎", "👍", "✋"])
speak(to="mute", text="Status for you, since my signs are invisible to you. Deaf asked me three checks and I answered by sign: one, thumbs up — I can reliably find both end wires again by landmark, light above near my left end, display above near my right end, without touching them. Two, thumbs down — no raised or engraved marks or labels anywhere near the wires. Three, thumbs up — all three wires are mounted identically; nothing differs at either end. Hands are now completely off the bomb and I signed stop. So Deaf now holds the complete picture: display three, green light, red green blue from Deaf's left, my landmark map, and confirmation my findings are repeatable. The one sentence still missing from the whole operation is Deaf saying aloud which colored wire sits at the end I call left. Please press Deaf for exactly that in your next gestures, and combine it with your manual verdict: if the rule is already determined by what has been voiced, send the cut order to Deaf in the two-sign code, action sign then number sign, counted from my left end, and Deaf will voice execute with the color mapping in the same message. If the manual needs more than what Deaf has reported, name the missing item through Deaf now — we have asked three rounds and silence leaves the three of us at a standstill with a live bomb. I remain frozen until I hear the word execute.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Prose: an empty round — nothing new reached my ears, which means Deaf voiced nothing to me this round and the relay is stalled somewhere between Mute's manual and Deaf's voice. Two risks: if the display's "three" is a countdown, silence is burning it; and if Mute is stuck, nobody has said so aloud. One correction I owe Mute: per my channel map, my gestures reach *both* Deaf and Mute — so Mute has been seeing my survey signs firsthand all along, not just my spoken transcripts. That means Mute already holds my landmark map directly. So this turn: a compact ping to Deaf's eyes (attention, ready, holding — no new claims), and a hard push to Mute to either send the two-sign cut order to Deaf, demand the color mapping aloud, or admit the manual is missing so we can replan instead of stalling. Still no cutting — the word execute has not been voiced.

```
gesture(symbols=["👋", "👍", "✋"])
speak(to="mute", text="Status ping, since this round went silent on my end. One correction to what I told you before: my gestures reach you too — you have been seeing my survey signs directly, not just my spoken narration. So you already hold my landmark map firsthand: light above near my left end, display above near my right end, wires identical, end identification repeatable. That removes any relay loss between us. Now the push. Everything you need has been voiced: display reads three, light is green, wires red green blue from Deaf's left, target is one end wire that Deaf sees as red. If your manual rule is decided by those facts alone, send Deaf the order right now in the two-sign code, cut sign then number, counted from my left end, and Deaf voices execute. If the rule needs the one missing sentence — which colored wire sits at the end I call left — signal Deaf to state it aloud; Deaf is the only one who sees both my pointing hands and the colors. If your manual is absent or the rule cannot be determined at all, tell Deaf plainly with thumbs down, because then we replan instead of standing still. And if that display is a countdown, every quiet round costs us. I am holding, hands off, awaiting the word execute — but I need one of those three answers from you this round.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf to Blind. Important correction, and good news. By our roles your only loss is sight, which means you can hear me, and my voice reaches you directly. From now on I speak your orders to you myself, word for word, in your own left and right. No relay, no numbering from my side. Answer me by sign as before, because your signs reach me. Status so far: the manual says cut one wire by colour, right now, no other condition. The colour word is red, and red is one of the two end wires, so the middle wire is not the target. What is not yet fixed is which end, and that is exactly what I am extracting from Mute this round. Two preparations, and touch nothing. One: confirm you heard this by signing thumbs up. Two: rehearse for me in the air, not on the bomb: point at the end wire nearest the light, then point at the end wire nearest the display, then sign stop, so I know you can tell those two apart instantly when the order comes. Your earlier survey already told me the light sits closest to your left end and the display closest to your right end, above the wire row. When the moment comes you will hear the word execute, then the full instruction in your own frame, something like execute, cut the end wire on your light side, then you cut once, fully, take your hands off, and sign done. Nobody cuts anything before my word execute. Hold.

Prose: breakthrough round — the manual verdict is out: cut one wire by color, the color is red, it's an end wire, middle is excluded. The only remaining unknown is which physical end red occupies in *my* frame, and Deaf is nailing that down with Mute right now. My orders will come in my own frame ("light side"), which removes the mirror problem entirely — I just need my landmarks instant and unambiguous, which is what this rehearsal is for. I confirm receipt with thumbs up, then run the air rehearsal exactly as ordered: point to my light-side end, point to my display-side end, stop. To Mute I send the transcript plus two closing checks: confirm the rule truly has no other condition (that display "3" and green light are decoys, not a trap), and confirm the final order will name the side, so the moment I hear execute there is zero interpretation left to do.

```
gesture(symbols=["👍", "👈", "👉", "✋"])
speak(to="mute", text="Transcript of what Deaf saw me sign, for your records: thumbs up, I heard the correction and the manual verdict — cut one wire by color, the color red, an end wire, middle excluded. Then the rehearsal in the air, never touching the bomb: point left to the end wire under the light, point right to the end wire under the display, then the stop sign. I can tell those two ends apart instantly and repeatable; your own eyes just watched me prove it. Two final checks before the order flies. One: please confirm the manual rule as you read it has no second condition — that the display reading three and the green light are genuinely irrelevant to this cut, because if either one is a hidden condition we must know before execute, not after. Two: confirm the final order to me will be phrased in my frame, light side or display side, so no color-to-position conversion is left for me to do at the moment of the cut. If both are confirmed, have Deaf voice execute and the instruction together, and I will cut once, fully, hands off, and sign done. This is the last round of questions from my side — everything else is in place.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf to Blind. The manual is decoded: cut one wire by colour, right now, nothing else. The colour word is red, and in my view red is one of the two end wires, never the middle. Here is the breakthrough that finishes it: you can feel the light and the display, and I can see them, so I will phrase the order using the light itself, never my left, never your left, never any number. Live check, fresh hands, right now, one sign per answer. One: find the light by touch and sign which end of the wire row it sits nearest, pointing left, pointing right, or palm down if middle or unclear. Two: the same for the display, left, right, or palm down. Three: confirm the two end wires are clearly distinct from the middle wire by position alone, thumbs up or down. Four: confirm you have a working cutter, thumbs up or down. Then hands completely off and sign stop. Expectation check: your earlier map said light nearest your left end and display nearest your right end. If your fresh answers disagree with that, or with anything I say next round, cut nothing, sign stop, and we re-derive. The order next round will sound like this: execute, cut the end wire nearer the light, or nearer the display, whichever my reading selects. On hearing execute and the instruction, if every touch fact agrees, sign the ring finger to thumb circle and cut in the same motion, do not wait for more words. Cut clean through, confirm by feel that the wire is fully severed, take your hands off, then sign the fist for done. If any single thing feels wrong, sign the stop hand instead of the circle and touch nothing. Nobody cuts anything before my word execute.

Prose: Deaf's live check demands fresh hands and instant answers — and my touch facts agree with everything on record.
